layers.long: Singapore: the oil-palm map marks about 38 ha inside the boundary (23 ha of them dated 1989, on Pulau Tekong). Singapore has no commercial oil palm, so these are most likely false positives; the details card does not report them.

layers.label: Pulpwood
layers.legend: Pulpwood — 2013–2015 snapshot (Spatial Database of Planted Trees), same for every month

layers.label: Peat
layers.legend: Peatland — areas with at least 30 cm of peat, modelled at about 125 m (CIFOR 2017, nominal 2011). Includes peat-forming mangroves (about 11 % of the tropical total). Not checked on the ground in Papua.
layers.title: Peat
layers.long: This peat map is modelled (CIFOR v2.1, Gumbricht et al. 2017) and is less reliable outside Indonesia and Malaysia, where it has not been checked against field data. Read hectares for other countries as "as mapped", not as ground truth.

layers.label: Burned area
layers.legend: Burned area — pixels with a burn date in the selected year, MODIS MCD64A1 (500 m). Faint at country scale: opacity = share of the area burned. Small fires and fires under thick smoke can be missed.
layers.title: Burned area (MODIS MCD64A1), year

layers.label: Forest history (TMF)
layers.legend: Forest history 1990 → selected year — humid tropical forest first cleared by that year (JRC TMF, 30 m). Purple = cleared before 2000 (this part is in every file), amber = cleared from 2000. 1990 shows everything cleared up to 1990.
layers.title: Forest history since 1990 (JRC TMF): deforestation

layers.label: Forest degradation (TMF)
layers.legend: Degraded forest — first logging or fire damage up to the selected year (JRC TMF). Degraded is not cleared: the canopy partly recovers or is cleared later. Files exist every 5 years (2000, 2005 … 2025): the nearest file at or before the selected year is shown. Light = before 2000, teal = 2000 onward.
layers.title: Forest history since 1990 (JRC TMF): degradation, every 5 years

layers.label: Converted to tree plantations (TMF)
layers.legend: Former forest now under tree plantations (end of 2025, JRC TMF). Includes oil palm, pulpwood, rubber and other tree crops; not only oil palm. Not tied to the selected year.
layers.title: Converted to plantation (JRC TMF: oil palm, pulpwood, rubber — not only oil palm)

layers.label: Forest loss then oil palm
layers.title: Forest loss → oil palm (lag between loss and planting)
layers.legend: Where Hansen forest loss (2001–2021) and Descals oil palm overlap, coloured by years from loss to planting (static, not tied to the selected year). Blue and purple = palm planted before the recorded loss (replanting or a timing offset). Overlap only: it does not show that fire or clearing caused the planting. Stronger colour = larger share of the map cell's area.
layers.gap_note: No dated plantation data in this country: forest loss followed by fire is shown, conversion to plantation is not assessed.

layers.label: What cleared forest became
layers.legend: What cleared forest became — Sims et al. 2025: the main reason forest was lost in each map cell (about 1 km across), one class for the whole of 2001–2025 (static, not tied to the selected year). Drawn only in cells where Hansen forest loss is recorded. Each class can be switched off.
layers.long: Each cell is about 1 km across and carries one class for the whole period 2001–2025, so a cell with several uses shows only its main one. Southeast Asia is one of the regions where the map is less accurate: about 71–83 % of cells are right there (the authors report 83 %; an unweighted check of their published validation points gives 71 %). The “wildfire” class was built using fire data, so it must not be read as independent evidence about fire.
layers.source: Sims et al. 2025, Global drivers of forest loss at 1 km resolution (v1.3), WRI / Google DeepMind. doi:10.5281/zenodo.19485190

layers.label: Oil palm (MapBiomas)
layers.title: Oil palm (MapBiomas)
layers.legend: MapBiomas Indonesia Collection 4 v2 (class 35 'oil palm'): share of each map cell (about 110 m) that became oil palm, shown from the year our rule says it first became oil palm, up to the selected year (stronger colour = larger share; clear = none). Data covers 2001 to 2023; later years show 2023.
important: This row shows land from the year our rule says it first became the class, and it only grows as the year moves. It is not MapBiomas' raw map of each year (that map can also shrink).
The 2001 value is inflated: much of it is oil palm the 2000 reference map did not show yet. Read 2001 as 'by 2001', not as a planting boom.
MapBiomas oil-palm area is about 12 % below the Descals oil-palm row, and there is almost no MapBiomas oil palm in the far east of Papua (141 to 144 E).
layers.long: Years are good to about plus or minus 2 years: each map cell (about 110 m) takes the median year of its changed 30 m pixels. A change counts only when the class holds for two years in a row, so the data stops at 2023 (later years show 2023) and the newest conversions are missing. Colour strength is the share of the cell that is the class at the end of 2023, shown from the cell's first year on. Land that was already the class in 2000 is not shown. Indonesia only. The 2001 value is inflated: much of it is oil palm the 2000 reference map did not show yet. MapBiomas oil-palm area is about 12 % below the Descals oil-palm row (and its first year is a median 1 year later than the Descals planting year); there is almost no MapBiomas oil palm in the far east of Papua (141 to 144 E) although Descals maps some.
layers.source: MapBiomas Indonesia Collection 4 v2, land use and land cover 2000-2024 (https://landy.mapbiomas.id), derived by us: first year a 0.001 degree cell became the class
